name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist and inventor of Atomic Layer Deposition technology.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: Researcher at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and author of this historical essay.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Finnish university where Suntola studied and later worked as an assistant teacher.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Finnish research organization where Suntola worked on humidity sensors before moving to industry.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical instrumentation company where Suntola invented Atomic Layer Epitaxy.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish building material and electronics company that acquired the ALE-EL project from Instrumentarium.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Company founded by Suntola to develop ALE technology for solar and semiconductor applications.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American competitor that acquired Lohja's EL business in 1990.

name: Neste Oy
summary: Finnish national oil company that established Microchemistry as a subsidiary.

name: ASM
summary: Dutch company that acquired Microchemistry in 1999.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: Company founded by former Microchemistry reactor designers, which Suntola joined after retirement.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Company that acquired Planar's EL plant in Olarinluoma in 2012.

name: Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Thin film growth technique based on repeated saturating gas-solid reactions invented by Suntola.

name: Humicap sensor
summary: Humidity sensor developed by Suntola and Antson at VTT before the ALE invention.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor at HUT who supervised Suntola's doctoral thesis and assigned the humidity sensor task.

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Colleague of Suntola who co-developed the Humicap sensor and co-invented ALE.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Close co-worker to Suntola in ALE reactor design since 1975 and co-founder of Picosun.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Colleague involved in the successful demonstration of the ZnCl2/H2S process.

name: Tampere
summary: City in Finland where Tuomo Suntola was born.

name: Finland
summary: Country where Suntola lived and developed ALE technology.

name: Espoo
summary: City in Finland where the ALE production facility was built.

name: Lohja
summary: City in Finland where pilot production of TF-EL displays started.

name: University of Leningrad
summary: Soviet university where Suntola visited Prof. Aleskovskii in 1990.

name: Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet researcher who independently discovered molecular layering in the 1960s.

name: SEMI
summary: Industry association that awarded Suntola the European SEMI Award in 2004.
